subject: Request: SOC2 Type II + targeted auth artifacts (token revocation & access review)
messages_1_headers:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@healthcore.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: security@healthcore.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: SOC2 Type II + targeted auth artifacts (token revocation & access review)
messages_1_body:
Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this — HealthCore is running a controls review ahead of a customer procurement window and we need your SOC 2 Type II report plus a small set of targeted artifacts to close a handful of controls. To be explicit, we need: 

- SOC 2 Type II report for the most recent period (report and cover/bridge letter).
- A bridge letter explicitly stating whether there were any control exceptions in the audit period and the covered audit dates.
- Token lifecycle policy & a sample revocation log (for admin-issued API tokens) — 30-day slice around any rotation event if available.
- Evidence of a recent privileged-access recertification (access review summary and the resulting remediation ticket list).
- Authn/authorization log slice (event types: login, MFA challenge, token_issue, token_revoke) for 2026-11-01 through 2026-11-14 (CSV or pre-filtered export).

We appreciate redwood's standard artifacts, but those specific items are gating controls for the procurement review. Our deadline for closing this packet is COB 2026-11-30 (we're aiming to circulate the packet to procurement on 12/1). If you can confirm scope and any constraints by EOD tomorrow, that would be very helpful.

If the log slice or revocation stream is sensitive, we can accept pseudonymized records and an accompanying statement about retention and access controls. Also, if SOC 2 bridge wording is preferred over a full re-issue, that is acceptable as long as it confirms the audit period and exceptions (if any).

Thanks — let me know if this needs to be routed elsewhere.

-Maya
Maya Patel
Security Operations Manager, HealthCore
maya.patel@healthcore.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
messages_2_headers:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@healthcore.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2 Type II + targeted auth artifacts (token revocation & access review)
messages_2_body:
Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list and the timeline.

Quick confirmations and constraints from our side: 
- SOC 2 Type II report: we will provide the 2026-09-30 period Type II report and a bridge letter stating the covered period and any exceptions (if applicable).
- Token revocation logs & token lifecycle policy: we can provide the policy doc and a redacted slice of the revocation events. The revocation stream contains user identifiers and service principals; we will pseudonymize user identifiers unless you need raw identifiers and an NDA addendum is in place.
- Privileged access recertification: we have an access review summary and remediation ticket list (Jira IDs redacted as needed).
- Authn log slice (2026-11-01 to 2026-11-14): we can export pre-filtered CSV with event types you listed, plus hashes for PII fields. Runbooks and brief notes on log retention will be included.

Plan: Markus (SRE) and Naomi (Trust) are cc'd — Markus will pull the log slices and token events; Naomi will coordinate the SOC2 artifacts and bridge language. We expect to deliver a secure Share link with artifacts and the CSV by 2026-11-26 EOD Pacific, subject to redaction confirmation. If you need an earlier partial deliverable, we can send the SOC2/bridge first.

A couple of clarifying questions: 
1) Do you require timestamps to be in UTC or local (we can supply both, default will be UTC)?
2) For the revocation slice, are you comfortable with pseudonymized subject identifiers (hash:salt) or do you require original emails/service names?

I'll follow up once Markus confirms extraction windows.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0789
messages_3_headers:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: SOC2 Type II + targeted auth artifacts (token revocation & access review)
messages_3_body:
FYI — pulling the requested slices now. Notes below and actions: 

On Tue, Nov 24, 2026 at 10:48 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick confirmations and constraints from our side:
> - SOC 2 Type II report: we will provide the 2026-09-30 period Type II report and a bridge letter stating the covered period and any exceptions (if applicable).
> - Token revocation logs & token lifecycle policy: we can provide the policy doc and a redacted slice of the revocation events...

Extraction notes (Markus):
- Authn logs: will export events (login, mfa_challenge, token_issue, token_revoke) for 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z through 2026-11-14T23:59:59Z as CSV. Fields: event_time (UTC), event_type, subject_hash, service, result, ip_country (if available), user_agent. PII (email/user id) will be hashed with per-request salt; we will include the salt metadata in the delivery enclave.
- Token revocation: the stream is split across two services (auth-svc and token-service). I'll provide a combined CSV with revocation_reason and policy_reference IDs. Where revocation ties to a privileged admin operation, we'll mark as PRV=true.
- Privileged access recertification: Naomi will pull the access review summary and corresponding remediation tickets from Confluence/Jira. We will redact ticket text but include ticket IDs unless HealthCore prefers masked IDs.

Deliverables we will upload to a secure Share link: 
1) redwood-soc2-type2-2026.pdf (SOC 2 Type II)
2) bridge-letter-2026-11-01.pdf (signed bridge letter)
3) auth-log-sample-2026-11-01_to_2026-11-14.csv (hashed identifiers)
4) token-revocation-slice-2026-11.csv (redacted)
5) access-review-summary-2026.pdf + remediation-ids.csv

Constraints: full raw logs are not sharable outside Redwood without an executed NDA and defined transfer controls. If HealthCore requires raw identifiers, please confirm and we can route to Legal for a narrow data transfer agreement.

I'll start the exports now and post the secure link when ready.

-Markus
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

messages_4_body:
Hi Olga / Markus / Naomi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity on constraints. The proposed deliverables and pseudonymization approach work for our risk team. Two small asks before you upload: 

1) Please provide timestamps in UTC (that will simplify our ingestion).
2) For the salt metadata used in hashing, include a short note describing the hashing function (sha256) and salt handling — we won't need the salt value itself, just the method so our team can validate uniqueness assumptions.

If you can get the secure link to us by EOD 11/26 (Pacific), we'll proceed with our controls review and aim to get procurement aligned for 12/1. If anything changes on our side, I'll let you know immediately.

Best regards,
Maya
Maya Patel
Security Operations Manager, HealthCore
